Your team projects 69.0 with Haaland captained, a modest lead built on two strong players rather than depth. Salah and Haaland alone account for more than a third of that total; the rest of the eleven spreads fairly evenly between 4.1 and 6.1. The bench is thin—Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only meaningful cover—so your starting choices matter.

The recommended transfer is Wood to Watkins, netting 6.4 over the season ahead with no immediate cost. You have the budget and the free transfer available, so the question is whether to make it now or hold your flexibility.

Muniz carries a 50% chance of playing, which makes him unreliable as a fallback. If he doesn't start, you'd bring on Anderson (2.9), a small downside. That's manageable but worth watching.

Haaland holds the armband 0.3 clear of Salah, though the gap is tight. His ceiling is higher—8% odds of returning 2 or fewer points versus the baseline risk—but neither captain choice is wrong. The model backs Haaland; Salah remains a sensible alternative if you want to hedge.

Your team projects 60.8 this week with Haaland as captain. That edge over Salah is small — only 0.3 — so the armband choice hinges on risk tolerance rather than a clear signal; Haaland's ceiling is higher but his floor is lower.

The recommended transfer swaps Wood for Watkins, gaining 6.4 points over the horizon at no hit cost. Wood's bench role makes him dispensable, and you have the funds.

Two small concerns. Muniz on your bench is a 50% doubt, so if he doesn't play you're left with Anderson at 2.9 as your fourth outfield player. More pressingly, you're heavy on Arsenal (three players) and Manchester City (two), so any underperformance there compounds. That said, these are your strongest assets and the model sees no reason to move them.

After the transfer you'll have £0.5m banked with one free move left. Hold unless injuries emerge.

Your projected score is solid at 69.0 with the armband. Haaland as captain is a marginal call—only 0.3 ahead of Salah—but the model backs it. The captain carries real uncertainty though: an 8% chance he scores 2 or fewer, balanced against a 25% chance of 10+.

The transfer from Wood to Watkins gains 6.4 points with no hit cost, so it's worth doing. That's a clean upgrade.

Muniz is flagged as doubtful with a 50% chance of playing. He's on your bench projecting 2.4, so if he doesn't start, Mykolenko at 3.1 comes in—a marginal difference. The flag is worth monitoring closer to kickoff, but it's unlikely to matter much to your score.

You're carrying three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That's concentrated, but it reflects where the model sees value this week.
